Yes. The matching paper is VaLiDRec by Shutong Qiao and coauthors, which proposes variable-length, LLM-aligned semantic IDs for generative recommendation [1]. It builds semantic IDs directly from native LLM vocabulary tokens, lets identifier length adapt to item semantic complexity, and replaces autoregressive SID generation with token-set prediction and token-level item scoring [1]. The abstract says it outperforms strong baselines, improves zero-shot item cold-start, and is much faster at inference than LC-Rec [1].

Related variable-length semantic-ID papers differ in approach: one introduces adaptive-length IDs with a discrete variational autoencoder and Gumbel-Softmax under a probabilistic framework [2]; another learns variable-length tokenization based on item popularity using PIBA, hyperbolic residual quantization, and a soft length controller [3]; and CapsID uses soft capsule routing with confidence-driven SID termination [4].
